comps: Marks

Max 150: three pieces 30 each (90), scales and arpeggios 21, sight-reading 21, aural tests 18. Distinction 130-150, Merit 120-129, Pass 100-119 (a pass in each component is not required to pass overall).
Choosing pieces

Three pieces, one from each of Lists A (faster, technical agility), B (lyrical, expressive) and C (varied traditions/styles). Live piano (or brass, where listed) accompaniment required except for unaccompanied SOLO pieces and studies; max two unaccompanied solos; recorded accompaniment not allowed. Grades 1-3 may offer duets (DUET / DUET/PIANO). Arrangements/transcriptions must use the listed edition, other editions free. Grades 1-5 share some pieces across instruments (not Horn). Related-instrument option: one piece may be played on a related instrument (trumpet/cornet/E♭ soprano cornet/flugelhorn; trombone/bass trombone at Grades 6-8). Memory optional (no extra marks); da capo/dal segno observed, other repeats omitted unless very short; cadenzas not played. Brass Prep Test and no Initial grade for brass.

sections: Scales & technical work

Sight-reading
Short unaccompanied piece, 30 seconds to look through/try. 4 bars, 4/4 (and 3/4); dotted minims/minims/crotchets and rests; notes tongued only.
Aural & other tests
A clap pulse and say 2 or 3 time; B sing 3 two-bar echoes (major, tonic-mediant); C spot a pitch change (near beginning/end); D questions on dynamics and articulation.

Digital technical pathway: 3 pieces x22 (66) + technical work 14 + overall performance 20 (delivery & focus 10, musical awareness 10); technical work is one unit, candidate chooses scales set A or B (memory) or two exercises (different groups) or two extracts; digital Repertoire-only pathway: 4 pieces x25 (8/8/9 components) = 100. Lip flexibility exercise notation is in the syllabus/Trinity brass resources (not reproduced here).
Choosing pieces

Three pieces from the current repertoire list (trinitycollege.com/brass): two accompanied from group A and one unaccompanied from group B (digital Repertoire-only: four pieces, at least two A and one B). Initial-Gr3: one group A piece may be a duet (horn, trumpet, cornet, flugelhorn, euphonium, baritone, trombone only; play upper part, duet partner on a brass instrument, no piano). Own composition allowed instead of a listed piece (accompanied replaces A, unaccompanied replaces B; must be notated, on stave at Gr6-8; durations 0.5-1 min Initial rising to 3.5-5 min Gr8). Bb trumpet: related instrument allowed for one piece from Gr3. Eb soprano cornet may choose pieces from tenor horn list (and vice versa Gr6-8); bass trombone may swap group B for trombone group B. None: no theory or lower-grade prerequisite for any grade.
Digital exams

Digital graded exams (from Dec 2024) are filmed as one continuous take and offer two pathways: Technical work pathway (3 pieces, technical work, overall performance; no sight reading/aural/improvisation/musical knowledge, replaced by overall performance marks) or Repertoire-only pathway (4 pieces). sections: Scales & technical work

Lip flexibility exercise (Gr8, memory) then EITHER Set A (2 oct, pace 88-132): C major (f slurred), F# minor (p tongued), chromatic on F# or C# (mf tongued), dom 7th in B (f slurred), dim 7th on C (mf tongued), augmented arpeggio on F# (p tongued); OR Set B: F# major (mf tongued), C minor (f slurred), whole-tone on F# (f slurred), dom 7th in F (p tongued), dim 7th on F# (f slurred), augmented arpeggio on C (p slurred); OR two extracts (as Gr6 rules): Trumpet: Bruckner Sym 7 mvt 1 (2nd trumpet in F, bars 139-149); Leoncavallo Pagliacci Act 2 sc 1 (1st trumpet in E, with repeat); Stravinsky Petrushka (trumpet in Bb). Sight reading: unseen extract, 30s prep, approx two grades lower than the exam. Parameters: two octaves plus one note, duplets, changing time signatures; transposed at Gr6-8 (C major read for C trumpet).

Two tests (10 marks each): sight reading (mandatory; two octaves plus one note, duplets, changing time signatures) plus either aural or improvisation (16 bars (C#/F minor, 5/4, 7ths/9ths/suspensions)). Trumpet candidates sight read transposed (C major read as C trumpet, up a tone; examiner plays first note); cornet/flugelhorn standard. comps: Entry requirement

Format & marks

Face-to-face (public venue or private visit) OR digital (video recorded at a time and place of the candidate's choice, with no fixed sessions; video uploaded at booking or within 28 days). General notes

General notes

No Grade 8 or Theory of Music prerequisite for any performance diploma (Trinity entry-requirements page and March 2026 syllabus). Current documents: 'Classical Music Performance Diplomas' syllabus, online edition March 2026 (resource id 8556, same for all instruments; Trinity points to trinitycollege.com/performance-diplomas for the current version) and 2026-edition instrument repertoire lists. Digital diplomas (ATCL, LTCL) allow recorded/backing-track accompaniment; face-to-face exams need a live accompanist. Own-choice programme approval: whole programme only, usually within 15 working days; the syllabus says the approval letter is valid 3 years, while a support article says 2 years (conflict, check the letter). Works on any current Trinity grade, certificate or lower-diploma list cannot be own-choice, and a work approved for one diploma cannot be reused at a higher diploma. Up to 30 s allowance for unshortened introductions/tuttis; gaps between movements about 10 s. General rules (all instruments)

Applies to all instruments. Performance times cover all works including short breaks between movements (about 10 seconds maximum) but not between works; the minimum has no leeway and under-length recitals are referred and penalised, while over-length ones may be curtailed. Programmes show a range of moods, styles and tempi. Use only one instrument type (family members such as flute and piccolo allowed; for flute at most one piece on piccolo or alto flute). Unaccompanied works may make up to 40% of an accompanied programme (one long listed work above 40% is accepted); pieces published with accompaniment may not be played unaccompanied; the candidate provides one accompanist (normally). Repeats: observe da capo and dal segno but do not play exposition or recapitulation repeats, repeats of more than two bars, or repeats within variations (Baroque suite repeats are allowed only if musically justified by ornamentation). Long introductions, endings and tuttis must be shortened (up to 30 seconds allowed). All cadenzas should be played. Memory is not required and earns no marks; metronomes and spoken introductions are not allowed. Music must be from a reliable, unaltered edition and legal copies are needed (copies for the examiner, and originals shown). Stagecraft is marked. A written programme (names, date, composers, full titles with movements and opus numbers, timing per piece and total, in order) is required.
Other components

Programme and planning section requires a written programme with programme notes on every piece totalling 1,200-1,600 words (musical and historical context, structure and form, significant musical elements; sources must be credited and not plagiarised). The balance and order of the programme are also judged. No viva or quick study.
